Description: Katniss mentions leaving the rabbit near the sleeping bags at the end of the cave, but this occurs before they have actually walked back to the cave. The text states 'I leave the rabbit near the sleeping bags at the end of the cave, to keep it safe while we prepare the fireplace' while they are still at the stream, before the sentence 'It's a long walk back to the cave, though.'

Katniss's mother is characterized as hating to take care of her daughters, which contradicts her established character as a devoted healer and mother who has been caring for them throughout the series.

The text describes a device on a table that 'caughts' (catches) attention and is 'beeping with the rythm of the bird's wings.' This is grammatically incorrect ('caughts' should be 'catches' or 'caught', 'rythm' should be 'rhythm') and creates a logical inconsistency - a device cannot beep in rhythm with hummingbird wings that beat 60-80 times per second, as this would be an impossibly fast beeping sound indistinguishable from a continuous tone.

Finnick is described as lying down on his bed while watching television with Katniss, but Katniss is in a hospital bed and Finnick brings his tray to her bed to watch together, suggesting they should be in the same location (her bed area), not separate beds.

Katniss thinks 'I wrap my arms tightly around his neck, thinking that soon I'll have to say good-bye to Gale. Instead he pulls me in close...' This suggests she hasn't yet said goodbye to Gale, but in the previous chapter (40), she was taken directly to the train without the traditional goodbye period, meaning she already failed to say goodbye to Gale before boarding the train.

Katniss refers to Clove as 'the girl from District 2' in her dream, but in Chapter 21, Clove was explicitly identified by name when she attacked Katniss at the feast. Katniss would know her name, not just her district.
